title: OpenCove outbound playnotes (cold-to-pilot)
content:
Quick context:
- Prospect: OpenCove (mid-market retail marketplace). Headquartered in Boston, ~320 employees, heavy e‑comm + 3rd-party logistics integrations. Tech: React front-end, Python microservices, existing search + rules engine on ElasticSearch.
- Why them: lots of SKU variety, slow search relevancy + cart abandonment spikes during promotions. They surfaced: inconsistent search latency and ops cost for rerank / personalization.
- Opportunity hypothesis: Start with a narrow pilot – product detail & checkout assistant that reduces support tickets and improves conversion. Low-friction POC using Redwood Hosted or Dedicated depending on data needs.

Account research notes (public + signals):
- Found 3 engineering talks from OpenCove Eng on SRE and scaling (good signal they instrument latency).
- Job posts show multiple search/ML engineer roles open (signal they care about relevance).
- Crunchbase: last funding Series B (2023), runway for experimentation but procurement cycles ~8–12w for vendor pilots >$50k.
- Security: they call out SOC2 on careers page but no published public cloud compliance doc — assume standard enterprise checks.

Key contacts (to source):
- Director of Search: likely person to engage for relevance pilot (target outreach first).
- Head of Product (marketplace).
- Lead SRE / Infra (for latency/SLAs).
- CS/ops owner for conversions & KPIs.
(Work to do: find names + LinkedIn roles, add to outreach cadences)

Pain / buying signals to surface in outreach:
- "Search slow during promos" -> tie to Redwood latency SLO + prefix caching
- "Rising cost on tokens/ops" -> Redwood Optimize ideas: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions
- "Need predictable capacity for peak sales" -> Redwood Dedicated offerings and burst capacity
- "Compliance / data concerns" -> Redwood Private (VPC) + KMS/HSM option

Value props to call out (short bullets for subject lines / intros):
- Production latency guarantees for interactive search and assistant flows
- Automatic KV/prefix caching to cut per-token cost without UX hit
- Dedicated pools for promo windows + automatic fallback to hosted if needed
- Developer-first SDKs → fast integration with existing React/Python stack

Outbound sequence (drafts):
1) Short cold email (subject + 1 liner):
   Subject: Quick idea to cut search latency & boost promo conversion
   Hi <Name>,
   Noticed OpenCove has big promo spikes — simple wins that cut search latency (and checkout drops) by ~30–50% via caching + smarter batching. Can I share a 2‑week pilot plan?
   — Asha, Redwood Inference

2) Follow up (data + credibility):
   Subject: 2‑week pilot — sample plan + expected metric lift
   Hi <Name>,
   Quick supplement: we’ve run similar pilots for mid‑market marketplaces and saw 12–18% increase in conversion through faster, more relevant product suggestions and a 40% drop in tokens per session with KV caching. Attached a one‑pager. Is Wed/Thu for a 20min sync?

3) If no response: Slack/LinkedIn touch + intro to a short Loom demo of a mock query flow (30s).

Pilot scope (recommended low friction):
- Duration: 2 weeks + 2 weeks validation
- Goal: reduce median product search latency by 25% and improve add-to-cart conversion metric by 8–12%
- Surface: 1 vertical (home goods) + checkout assistant for 5 common cart questions
- Integration: client side calls to Redwood hosted endpoint + server side ephemeral logs (no PII ingestion)
- Exit: demo of results + ops playbook for Dedicated if scale/SLAs required

Estimated costs (ballpark for sizing comps):
- Hosted pilot: $5–8k for 4 weeks (dev effort + usage) — frame as low risk
- Dedicated baseline (if they want isolation): ~$10–25k/mo depending on burst and slot sizes (need infra input to refine)

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We already have Elastic/Seldon/LLM infra" -> acknowledge and propose hybrid: keep ES for retrieval + Redwood for scoring/serving to avoid rip-and-replace. Show ease of integration via SDK.
- "Cost concerns" -> talk about unit economics: batching, KV caching, prefix caching reduce per-session token spend; show Optimize recommendations from prior case. Offer trial credits.
- "Security/compliance" -> explain Redwood Private + VPC, KMS/HSM options and SOC2 mention. Offer an NDA and outline preliminary security questionnaire responses.
- "Procurement takes long" -> offer a low-dollar PO pilot or paid pilot agreement template; show flexible contract: month-to-month pilot + SLA addendum only if scaling.

Cold call script (20–30s opener):
- "Hi <name>, this is Asha at Redwood. We help marketplaces make search and checkout assistants faster and cheaper — two quick wins we typically show in a week. Can I book 20 minutes to show a narrow pilot plan that doesn't touch your core search stack?"

Emails / assets to prepare before outreach:
- One‑pager tailored to OpenCove with notes on their traffic pattern and suggested verticals (create and attach)
- Loom: 60–90s mock flow for product search + checkout assistant (mock data)
- Pilot contract template + low‑dollar SOW for procurement
- Security one‑pager (SOC2 + Private options)

Analytics / metrics to promise and measure in pilot:
- Median and p95 latency for search queries
- Tokens per session (to validate cost reductions)
- Conversion rate (add-to-cart) for target vertical
- Support ticket volume for checkout questions

Open questions / follow-ups (todo):
- Find actual names/emails for Director of Search + Head of Product (LinkedIn scrape)
- Get baseline metrics: current median/p95 search latency, current conversion numbers by vertical (ask CS/ops in discovery)
- Validate if they have a vendor policy that blocks hosted endpoints (procurement)
- Ask infra for a Dedicated slot quote for a promo weekend (ballpark)

Next steps (this doc owner):
- Today: draft OpenCove one‑pager + Loom prototype (Asha)
- Tue: feed to Priya for copy review; Liam to mock a simple curl example for integration
- Wed: target first outreach to Director of Search (cold email + LinkedIn)

Notes to self: keep messaging concrete — engineers care about latency & cost numbers more than "AI" buzzwords. Use specific examples ("30% latency cut, 40% token reduction") and avoid vague promises.

Scratch / snippets for quick paste into email or Slack:
- "We can run a narrow 2‑week pilot that integrates in under a day and shows latency + cost delta — no change to your retrieval layer required."
- Pain callout: "Promo weekends spike p95 latency by X, we can cut tail latencies with caching + dedicated slots."
- Ask: "Do you have a pilot budget or would a low-dollar trial PO work for procurement?"

End.
